source.note: Traefik publishes NO per-version Kubernetes compatibility matrix — supportWindows is deliberately NULL, unlike Istio's supportStatus.yml-derived rows. What it does publish is a ROLLING policy (docs/content/includes/kubernetes-requirements.md, every tag since v3.0.0): Traefik "supports at least the latest three minor versions of Kubernetes" (1.35–1.37 on 2026-10-10), plus the Helm chart's hard floor kubeVersion >=1.25.0-0 (chart 41.7.1, appVersion v3.7.14); neither is a per-add-on-version row, so neither is transcribed as a supportWindow. The two prose floors are EndpointSlices (k8s >=1.21, v3.1) and the */v1beta1 removal (k8s >=1.22, v3.0), both below every supported EKS version. The forced hop is therefore LIFECYCLE, not Kubernetes: 3.7 is the only supported line (3.6 security support ended 2026-08-16, 2.11 2026-09-07). latestKnownVersion is 3.7.14 (the newest committed release tag — a PATCH, because the 3.7 rules carry introducedIn patches and "3.7" told every 3.7.x install it was current) so the analyzer can still compute a currency hop (installed -> latest known release) for rule selection; this hop is NOT a Kubernetes-compatibility claim and every surface that renders it must say so (see AddonCompatAnalyzer.HopReason.CURRENCY). rules and upgradeNotes are deliberately EMPTY: unlike the hand-curated add-ons, Traefik's breaking changes are transcribed into kb/traefik/notes-*.md and evaluated through the generated-rules pipeline (sourceId 'traefik'), exactly like Istio. Detection: a single bare 'traefik' image suffix matches every observed repo path (docker.io/traefik official, ghcr.io/traefik/traefik, rancher/mirrored-library-traefik on k3s/RKE2 — confirmed live via ClickHouse: cluster_88613846051f runs rancher/mirrored-library-traefik:3.6.13) because 'traefik' is a distinctive brand name; it does NOT match traefik-hub or traefikee (neither repo path ends in the literal substring 'traefik'). Traefik Hub (hub.traefik.io, a separate commercial product with its own CRD group) is deliberately NOT fingerprinted here — it would need its own add-on entry, never evidence for this one.
